item.description: Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim Ahmed Ibrahim criticized the United States Monday for failing to issue a visa to Army Chief Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan to attend the U.N. General Assembly, while calling for an end to foreign support fueling the country’s civil war.

item.title: BBC Africa: Journalist to be crowned king in Uganda after bitter succession dispute
item.description: Kijanangoma is being crowned amid a dispute over a young heir whom the royal clan does not recognise.

item.title: BBC Africa: Two mass shootings in South Africa leave 28 dead
item.description: The two attacks hours apart come as the country struggles to stop high levels of gang-related armed violence.

item.title: Africanews: Pope Leo ends France trip in Metz, spotlighting Schuman and EU unity
item.description: Pope Leo XIV ended his four-day visit to France in Metz on Monday by urging Europe to build on its Christian heritage and culture of dialogue rather than succumb to what he called the “desire for domination” behind many of today’s wars.

item.title: Africanews: UN marks 25 Years of Durban Declaration as Guterres calls for stronger global action
item.description: The UN General Assembly marked 25 years of the Durban Declaration on racism and racial discrimination with a high-level meeting in New York.

item.title: Africanews: DRC: Vally Amisi’s Family Demands Answers [Africanews Today]
item.description: In the DRC, Vally Amisi’s family is demanding answers. In Ethiopia, fears of renewed conflict are growing among the population, while Niger takes back control of its uranium sector.

item.title: Africanews: Three migrants die in Channel crossing as boats become more overcrowded and risky
item.description: Emergency crews gathered at the port of Calais after three migrants died trying to cross the English Channel to Britain. Two women in their thirties and a 10-year-old boy, believed to be Eritrean, died in what appears to have been a crush aboard an overcrowded dinghy.

item.title: BBC Africa: Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July. Here's what we know so far
item.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa says the murders are a "stain on our national conscience".

item.title: Africanews: Traoré marks four years in power, following Sankara’s legacy
item.description: Captain Ibrahim Traoré has now led Burkina Faso for four years, the same length of time Thomas Sankara was in power.

item.title: BBC Africa: Remains of dozens of suspected kidnap victims found in Nigerian forests
item.description: Investigations are ongoing to establish the identities of at least 28 people whose remains were recovered by police.

item.title: Africanews: Ethiopia fighting intensifies as Government forces retake Alamata
item.description: Fighting is intensifying in northern Ethiopia, with pro-government forces saying they have retaken the strategic town of Alamata in southern Tigray.

item.title: Africanews: Kenya’s Quakers are using song and dance to keep younger generations in church
item.description: Kenyan Quakerism has always set itself apart with its use of music but lately, it has had to adapt to attract younger worshippers, with faster songs and modern instruments.

item.title: BBC Africa: Injured Assefa narrowly misses world record in Berlin
item.description: Ethiopian runner Tigst Assefa wins the Berlin Marathon but narrowly misses out on breaking the women's world record because of injury.

item.title: BBC Africa: Nigerian attempts to break world record by dancing non-stop for seven days
item.description: Crowds have gathered in Lagos to watch Ben Dancer, who says he will carry on dancing until Wednesday morning.

item.title: BBC Africa: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
item.description: Exploring the issues behind the escalation of tensions between the TPLF and the national army.

item.title: Africanews: Sudan rejects Ethiopia’s claims of backing Tigray forces
item.description: Sudan’s military is rejecting accusations from Ethiopia that Khartoum is backing armed groups fighting government forces in the north, calling the claims “baseless.”

item.title: BBC Africa: Why are Ethiopia's rebels joining forces?
item.description: Seven rebel groups from across Ethiopia have announced a new alliance against Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government.

item.title: BBC Africa: Families welcome guilty verdict over Mali crash that killed 116
item.description: Relatives of the victims tell the BBC they are relieved to finally have a ruling 12 years after the crash.
